decisive_items: Regular rhythm with cannon A waves in the jugular venous waveform
QRS complexes outnumber P waves with 3:2 relationship
P-wave morphology shows negative deflection in leads II and aVF
response.rationale: Only AVNRT can explain a regular narrow-complex tachycardia with cannon A waves, retrograde P waves negative in II/aVF, and ventricular activations outnumbering atrial activations due to retrograde block. The other candidates require 1:1 AV conduction or more atrial than ventricular activations.

rejected.why: Atrial flutter would show atrial activations outnumbering QRS complexes, not QRS outnumbering P waves; cannon A waves are not characteristic.
Atrial tachycardia would have P waves equal to or exceeding QRS complexes; QRS outnumbering P waves and cannon A waves are inconsistent.
Orthodromic AVRT requires a 1:1 AV relationship; the 3:2 ventricular-to-atrial relationship excludes it.
